entries.title: Fontshare
entries.description: Free, properly good typefaces from the Indian Type Foundry. My first stop when a client has no font budget but still deserves something with character.
entries.why: free fonts for client work and logo exploration

entries.title: Google Fonts
entries.description: The big open-source font library. Filter by variable fonts and language support before falling in love with anything.
entries.why: web fonts with Devanagari support

entries.title: Butterick's Practical Typography
entries.description: A whole book about typography for people who write, free online. The chapters on line length and font pairing settle most arguments.
entries.why: send to clients who want everything in bold

entries.title: Type Scale
entries.description: Pick a base size and a ratio and it previews the whole heading scale live. Saves me from guessing h2 sizes for the hundredth time.
entries.why: setting up a type ramp for a new site

entries.title: Fonts In Use
entries.description: An archive of real typography in the wild, searchable by typeface. The quickest way to see if a font looks good on a logo, a poster or a book cover before buying it.
entries.why: checking a typeface on real logo work

entries.title: Coolors
entries.description: Press space, get a palette. Lock the colours you like and keep spinning until something clicks. Embarrassingly addictive.
entries.why: quick palette starting points

entries.title: Realtime Colors
entries.description: Try a palette on an actual website layout instead of on swatches. Text, background, primary, secondary and accent, all live.
entries.why: showing a client a palette in context

entries.title: OKLCH Color Picker
entries.description: A colour picker and converter for OKLCH, the colour space where lightness actually behaves. Good for building tints that look evenly spaced.
entries.why: making perceptually even colour ramps

entries.title: Contrast Ratio
entries.description: Paste two colours, get the WCAG contrast ratio. Tiny, fast, and handles transparency, which most checkers ignore.
entries.why: accessibility check before handoff

entries.title: Laws of UX
entries.description: Short, beautifully illustrated cards on the psychology behind interfaces: Hick's law, Fitts's law, Jakob's law and friends. Great for backing up a design decision in a review.
entries.why: explaining why a button should be bigger

entries.title: Refactoring UI
entries.description: Practical tactics for making interfaces look better without being a designer, which is useful even when you are one. Spacing, hierarchy and shadows explained plainly.
entries.why: fixing a dashboard that looks off

entries.title: 10 Usability Heuristics for User Interface Design
entries.description: The classic ten rules for usable interfaces from Nielsen Norman Group. Old, unglamorous, still right about almost everything.
entries.why: heuristic review of an app

entries.title: Mobbin
entries.description: A huge library of real app screens and flows, searchable by pattern. Onboarding, paywalls, settings, empty states: someone has already shipped it.
entries.why: seeing how real apps do onboarding

entries.title: Design Systems Repo
entries.description: A directory of public design systems, pattern libraries and style guides from companies big and small. Handy when naming components.
entries.why: comparing how others name components

entries.title: Brand New
entries.description: Reviews of new logos and identity redesigns, with before and after. The comments are half the fun.
entries.why: keeping up with identity redesigns

entries.title: Logo Design Love
entries.description: A long-running blog about logo and identity design, full of process stories and sketches. Calm, generous and never trendy.
entries.why: process references for logo work

entries.title: SVGOMG
entries.description: Drop in an SVG, get a much smaller one. Toggle each optimisation and watch the preview so nothing breaks. Every logo export goes through here.
entries.why: cleaning up logo SVG exports

entries.title: siteInspire
entries.description: A slow, well-curated showcase of web design, filterable by style and subject. Less noise than the big galleries.
entries.why: mood board for a portfolio site

entries.title: Lapa Ninja
entries.description: A gallery of landing pages sorted by category, with whole sections on pricing pages, hero sections and footers. Scroll here before designing any SaaS pricing table.
entries.why: pricing page and landing page references

entries.title: Savee
entries.description: A visual bookmarking app full of other designers' saves. Rabbit hole warning: you go in for one reference and come out with forty.
entries.why: collecting visual references for a pitch

entries.title: Bartosz Ciechanowski
entries.description: Long interactive essays explaining how things work, from mechanical watches to GPS, with hand-built 3D demos. The gold standard for explaining with visuals.
entries.why: proof that explainers can be beautiful

entries.title: A Dao of Web Design
entries.description: The essay from 2000 that argued web pages should flow and adapt instead of copying print. Responsive design before it had a name.
entries.why: reminder that the web is not paper

entries.title: The Futur on YouTube
entries.description: Videos on the business side of design: pricing your work, talking to clients, branding. Good for long drives and pricing anxiety.
entries.why: how to price freelance work
